This is kinda a chan like forum where I use IPv6 to its absolute limit.

IPv6 attribute have been mapped to dictionary words so that when you visit, you get an automatic name based on your IPv6. That's just one goody. There are many others I've tried to build in.

If you're on IPv4, you can't use the site at all. You will get to the losers page and you will see other losers. The page is linked to from the about section too so IPv6 people can get to it.

I recommend you visit and play around and if you have suggestions for pushing IPv6 even more, lmk.

story_text.value:
The programming interview process can feel like a race to the bottom. To get ahead of the curve, we've decided to define what it looks like at the bottom.

Enter Hackerdome: a real time PvP programming puzzle duel with spectators and sabotage. A very non-serious site for a serious purpose (having a little more whimsy in our lives), where you can race a competitor to solve a programming puzzle or spectate and watch the chaos unfold. If the puzzles get too boring, the players might just find their editor playing back, with pop ups, font shifts, and more.

Enjoy!

title.value: Show HN: HackerDome, real time PvP programming duels ft. spectating and sabotage

story_text.value:
Hello HN!

We're building a single search/browse API interface to thousands of ecommerce stores (hopefully, eventually, all of them). Inspired by Shopify's https://shop.dev, we embedded a WASM bridge of our CLI in our website.

The idea is to provide an efficient commerce interface for agents; personal assistants (Instinct et al) or otherwise. The alternatives are to build a crawling system / Firecrawl, use an LLM search api (Exa, Parallel etc) or use embedded headless browsers. Collective action by brands/retailers to implement agentic-protocols (UCP, ACP etc) is unlikely; so we're doing it for them.

Surprisingly, despite our coverage list being smaller than Shopify's and the search endpoint being slower (~3k ms for p90; because there is JEV and/or LLM to convert free form search to facets) the search results are often subjectively better:

``` storerouter search 'gold frame pink tint sunglasses' --facet category_path.depth_3=sunglasses --facet temple_color=gold --facet lens_color=pink --facet eyewear_frame_material=metal ```

vs Shop.dev's: ``` shop search 'gold frame pink tint sunglasses' --category gid://shopify/TaxonomyCategory/aa-2-27 # dropped facet temple_color=temple_color__gold (no Shopify filter) # dropped facet lens_color=lens_color__pink (no Shopify filter) # dropped facet eyewear_frame_material=eyewear_frame_material__metal (no Shopify filter) # category 'sunglasses' → Apparel & Accessories > Clothing Accessories > Sunglasses ```

title.value: Show HN: Shop via CLI; for agents and software engineers
